The picture below is a photo of the accumulated snow on an earthen mound in an open area of the south campus of Handan No. 1 Middle School, taken on the twelfth day of the first lunar month; the accumulated snow had not been affected by human activities. <image1> Based on the phenomenon of accumulated snow shown in the picture, fill in the blank: the snow-line distribution phenomenon most similar in principle to this phenomenon is "the Alps ____ snow line is lower".
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the photo, there are multiple earthen mounds in the open area, and the white accumulated snow does not evenly cover all the slope surfaces, but is concentrated and retained on certain slope surfaces; some adjacent slope surfaces are darker in color, and the accumulated snow has basically melted. The question stem states that the accumulated snow was not affected by human activities, so this difference should mainly come from different slope aspects under natural conditions receiving heat differently and having different strengths of snowmelt. Then reason: Handan is located in the Northern Hemisphere, and in winter the sun is mainly toward the south; south-facing slopes receive stronger sunlight and obtain more heat, so the accumulated snow melts quickly; north-facing slopes are shady slopes, receive less heat, and the accumulated snow is easier to preserve. Transferring the principle that "accumulated snow is easier to preserve on shady slopes, and the snow line is lower" to the Alps, which are also in the Northern Hemisphere, it should be that the snow line is lower on the northern slope.
